sentences.text: This petition is filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1989 seeking compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- in respect of injuries sustained by him in the Road Traffic Accident.

2. It is the case of the petitioner that, on 28.07.2024 at about 5.30 pm petitioner was riding Electric Moped bearing Reg.No.KA-02-KY-1706 along with his son, near Nadgir College exit,
Tumkuru-Bengaluru NH-48 road, Madavara, Dasanapura Hobli, Bengaluru North Taluk,
Bengaluru, slowly by observing traffic rules.
At that time, a car bearing No.KA-04-MR-8974 driven by its driver came at high speed in rash and negligent manner, without observing the traffic rules dashed to the petitioner's moped.
Due to impact, petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

3. Immediately he was shifted to Premier Sanjeevini hospital, Bangalore and thereafter he was shifted to ESIC Medical College, PGIMSR & Model hospital, Bengaluru wherein he has taken treatment from 29.07.2024 to 05.08.2024.

entities.text: ESIC Medical College, PGIMSR & Model hospital, Bengaluru
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: It was found that petitioner sustained grievous injuries Type VI left volar barton fracture and other injuries.
He underwent surgery.
He has spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical expenses, conveyance food and nourishment.
Petitioner was an Electrician earning (SCCH-12) 3 MVC.
Due to this accident, he is unable to do any work as he was doing prior to the accident.
The accident is caused due to rash and negligent driving of driver of Car bearing No.KA-04-MR-8974.
The Nelamangala Traffic Police have registered case against the driver of the car bearing No.KA- 04-MR-8974 in Crime No.320/2024 U/Sec 125(a), 281 of BNS 2023.
The 1st respondent owner and 2nd respondent insurance company are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
On all these grounds, he prayed to allow the petition and award compensation.
4. 1st respondent is duly served.
He remained absent before this court.
Hence, he is placed ex-parte.
5. 2nd respondent insurance company appeared through its counsel and filed written statement denying the maintainability of case.

It has admitted the issuance of policy of private car package as on the date of accident, but denied the manner of accident, treatment taken by the petitioner,
accidental injuries caused to the petitioner and consequential disability alleged.
It is contended that there is one day delay in lodging the complaint which creates doubt about the involvement of insured vehicle in the accident.
The accident is caused due to the own negligence of the petitioner as he was riding the vehicle without wearing helmet.
That Sec.134 (C) and Sec.158(6) of MV Act is not complied.
On all these grounds 2nd respondent prayed to dismiss the petition.

6. On the basis of above pleadings, following issues are framed:-

1. Whether the petitioner proves that on 28.07.2024 at about 5.30 PM petitioner was riding Motor cycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-02-KY-1706 with his son near Nadgir Collage exit Tumakuru-Bengaluru NH-48 by observing traffic rules, at that time one car bearing Reg. No.KA-04-MR- 8974 driven by its driver in rash and negligent manner, without observing traffic rules, dashed to the petitioner's motor cycle and caused accident, due to which petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries as alleged?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so by whom and what is the quantum?
3. What Order or Award?
7. To prove his case, petitioner entered witness box and got examined as P.W.1.
Through his Ex.P.1 to P.9 documents are marked.
Dr.Ramesh.B- Orthopaedic Surgeon at Victoria hospital, Bangalore got examined as P.W.2.
Through him Ex.P.10 and 11 documents are marked and closed petitioner side evidence.
On respondent side not evidence is led.

8. Heard learned counsel for both sides and perused records.
9.

On taking into consideration the oral and documentary evidence placed before this Tribunal and arguments of both sides, I answer the above issues as follows: -
 Issue No.1: In the Affirmative,
 Issue No.2: Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3: As per final order,
 for the following;
 (SCCH-12) 5 MVC. No.6409/2024  REASONS 10. ISSUE NO.1 : It is stated that petitioner sustained grievous injuries in the RTA dt. 28.07.2024.

One Manoj Mistry who is said to be the son of petitioner has filed first information to Nelamangala Police stating that himself and his father petitioner herein were coming back from work at 5.30 in the evening.

At that time one Car tried to overtake the vehicle of the petitioner to go to service road drove the said vehicle in rash and negligent manner and dashed to the petitioner's vehicle due to which, both of them fell down and his father sustained grievous injuries.
The said car number is KA-04-MR-8974 Alto 800.
That his father was shifted to PGIMSR later he was shifted to ESIC hospital.
Therefore action may be taken against the said car driver.
The said first information is given to police on the next day of the accident i.e., 29.07.2024.

sentences.text: The spot panchanama is drawn which shows it is N.H-48 having 24ft tar road, 3 lane east-west direction.
The accident has taken place on the northern side of the road.
There is exit to service road at 10ft away.
As per IMV report both the aforesaid vehicles have sustained damages in which car has sustained right side front fender damage while the scooter has sustained damages on its front side.

As per the wound certificate produced at Ex.P.5 petitioner has sustained swelling, tenderness over left wrist, right elbow abrasion of 4 X 3 cms, right hand surface abrasion of 3 X 2 cms, right knee abrasion of 4 X 2 cms, left knee abrasion of 3X 1 cm.
X-ray shows fracture of distal end of left radius.
As per final report one Raghu driver of car bearing No.KA-04-MR-8974 is found to be negligent and charge sheet is (SCCH-12) 6 MVC. No.6409/2024 filed against him.
The said charge sheet is not questioned by the owner or driver of the car.
12. In the cross examination of P.W.1 petitioner denied negligence on his part.
Respondents have not led any evidence to show the negligence on part of petitioner, though such specific contention is taken in the written statement of respondent no.2.

In that view of matter based on the oral and documentary evidence, in the absence of any contrary evidence by the respondent side this court comes to the conclusion that driver of opponent car was rash and negligent in driving the vehicle.
Hence, this issue is answered in the Affirmative.
13. ISSUE NO.2 :
In the light of above reasons petitioner is entitled for compensation since 2nd respondent has admitted the insurance policy, he is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
To prove his age petitioner has produced D.L and aadhaar card at Ex.P.8 and 9 which shows his date of birth as 10.01.1973.
Accident took place on 28.07.2024.
He was aged 51 years at the time of accident.
Therefore, the age of the petitioner is considered as 51 years at the time of accident.
14. In respect of occupation it is stated that, he was an Electrician by profession and was earning Rs.40,000/- per month.
He has not produced any document to show his income.
Therefore notional income has to be considered.

Accident having taken place in the year 2024 the monthly income of the petitioner is held as Rs.16,500/-.
15.
In respect of permanent disability petitioner got examined Dr.Ramesh.B as P.W.2.
He is not a treated doctor.
He has (SCCH-12) 7 MVC. No.6409/2024 assessed only disability.
According to him petitioner had sustained fracture of distal radius left and fracture is united with implants in situ.
The P.W.2 doctor has assessed the permanent physical disability of left upper limb @32% and whole body disability @ 11%.
According to petitioner he was working as an Electrician the nature of injuries in the upper limb will affect his avocation.
Therefore, in the opinion of this court the functional disability affecting the income of the petitioner is 11%.

The quantum of compensation is determined as under:
(i) Medical expenses:

The petitioner took treatment at ESIC Medical college,
PGIMSR and model hospital.
No medical bills is produced by the petitioner.

Hence,
no compensation is awarded under this head.
(ii) Food and nourishment:
The petitioner underwent surgery for distal radius left as per discharge summary produced at Ex.P.7.

sentences.text: Rs.7X 500/- = Rs.3,500/- is awarded.

(iii) Attendant charges: Someone must have taken care of the petitioner during his treatment period.
Even if his own family member has taken care their per day income is lost hence for attendant charges Rs.7X500/- Rs.3,500/- is awarded.
(iv) Loss of income during laid up period: Minimum 2 months is required to recover from injury due to his advanced age.
Hence, his loss of income during laid up period is considered as Rs.33,000/-.
(v) Conveyance charges:
It is stated that petitioner took treatment at ESIC hospital.
He has spent money for conveyance (SCCH-12) 8 MVC. No.6409/2024 for the purpose of treatment.
Considering the same, this court is of the opinion that amount of Rs.3,000/- shall be awarded as conveyance charges.
(vi) Loss of future income due to Disability :
As per the findings given above, there is 11% functional disability affecting the income of the petitioner.

Hence, loss of future income due to disability is Rs.16,500/- income X 12 months X 11% disability X 11 multiplier to the age group of 51-55 which comes up to Rs.2,39,580/- compensation is awarded under this head.
(vii) For Future medical expenses:
As per the evidence of doctor there is need for future surgery for removal of implants but, no estimation is provided to that effect.
Hence amount of Rs.25,000/- is awarded for future medical treatment.
(viii) For Pain and sufferings:
The petitioner has sustained distal radius left.
Therefore, for pain and suffering the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.30,000/- .
(ix) Physical discomfort and loss of amenities of life : There is evidence of doctor to show that grievous injury has affected the normal life of the petitioner.
Therefore, compensation of Rs.40,000/- is awarded under this head.
(x) Loss of future prospect:

As per the judgments of the Hon'ble Supreme court, even in injury cases,
loss of future prospect has to be considered.
But in the present case, the on going through the evidence and the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner there is no chance of loss of future prospect.
Hence no compensation is awarded under this head.

16. ISSUE NO.4 : In view of above reasons I proceed to pass following;
ORDER The petition filed by the petitioner u/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.

It is held that, petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.3,77,580/- with interest @ 6% pa on Rs.3,52,580/-
from the date of petition till the date of payment.
(Future medical expenses of Rs.25,000/- will not carry interest).

Respondent No.2 being insurer of  opponent vehicle is liable to pay  compensation to the petitioner and hereby directed to deposit the aforesaid compensation amount with interest before this tribunal within two months from the date of this order.
